questions.s:
A laboratory assistant has a mixture of solid sulfur and solid carbon.
Sulfur is very soluble in carbon disulfide (boiling point 46 °C) and slightly soluble in water. Carbon is insoluble in both solvents.

A sample of the mixture is shaken with water. This is P.
Another sample of the mixture is shaken with carbon disulfide. This is Q.

Which procedure is used to prepare a pure sample of sulfur?
o: P is distilled and the distillate is evaporated to dryness to obtain sulfur.
P is filtered and the filtrate is allowed to evaporate to dryness to obtain sulfur.
Q is filtered and the residue is allowed to evaporate to dryness to obtain sulfur.
Q is filtered and the filtrate is allowed to evaporate to dryness to obtain sulfur.

property: going down the group, the boiling point of the halogens increases; reason: as molecular size increases, the intermolecular forces of attraction become stronger
